title: Heterogeneous pool provisioning for embeddings: tenant-aware hot/cold scaling
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Some tenants experience large, short-lived embedding bursts (search indexing, batch bulk-embed jobs) which either cause long tails (high p99 latency) when admitted, or wasted headroom when we overprovision. Current single-pool autoscaler is reactive and treats all tenants uniformly, resulting in noisy neighbor effects and inefficient GPU utilization.

Goal: Implement heterogeneous pool provisioning and tenant-aware admission control to reduce p99 latency during bursts, increase utilization by 10-20% on stable workloads, and provide predictable per-tenant SLAs. This ticket covers design, prototype, and canary plan for the autoscaler + queueing changes for embeddings routing.

Success metrics: average p95 token latency <= 70ms on 1k token inputs for priority tenants, p99 reduction >= 30% on burst windows, GPU utilization uplift >= 12% during baseline periods, no increase in error rate above 0.1% during rollout.

Scope:
- Heterogeneous GPU pools: define hot (low-latency, reserved headroom) and cold (high-throughput, best-effort) pools.
- Tenant classification: rules and heuristics to tag tenants as latency-sensitive, throughput-oriented, or batch-only.
- Admission & shaping: per-tenant concurrency limits, token-rate shaping, and preflight checks to route to appropriate pool.
- Predictive right-sizing: small ML model + moving-window traffic predictor to pre-warm hot pool capacity for scheduled bursts (e.g., nightly indexing).
- Observability: add per-tenant breakdowns, headroom metrics, and autoscaler decisions traces to Console.

Out of scope: embedding model optimization (quantization/kernels) and end-to-end retraining of tenants' workloads. Those are tracked in separate tickets.

comments: 2025-02-12 — Aisha: Created initial ticket after on-call incident where tenant X monopolized embedding pool for 18m causing p99 to spike. Attached incident summary and sample traces.

2025-02-18 — Marco: Spikes analysis complete. Identified two primary patterns: short burst spikes (few minutes) and scheduled bulk jobs (hour-scale). Proposed hot pool headroom target = 20% of recent peak per-hour demand for latency-sensitive tenants.

2025-02-25 — Eng: Prototype admission controller implemented. Uses token-bucket per-tenant with dynamic refill based on 5-min EWMA of request rate. Early test on staging reduced p99 by ~22% for mixed tenant set.
2025-03-01 — PM (Sofia Kim): Reviewed prioritization — requested that 'batch-only' tenants be auto-tagged from billing metadata and allowed to pre-warm cold pool when scheduled via API.

2025-03-03 — Ops: Canary started in us-west-2 with 18 tenants (mix of prod and dev). Observed initial regressions: cold-pool queue grew 30% during overnight bulk jobs; fixed by tuning queue drain concurrency. Follow-up PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routers/pull/432
2025-03-05 — Marco: Updated autoscaler knobs and added rollout plan into description. Next: finalize predictive prewarm model and add Console traces for autoscaler decisions.
